import Foundation

/// The catalog rows of `get_media_analysis` (spec §11 CJ-25; road map
/// "creator-jobs" CJ2a; `masks` CO-14, `faces` CJ-34, `sound_events` FC-33,
/// `subjects` VR-14) and `split_at_shots`
/// (CJ-29, CJ2b), spliced in by `creatorTools()`.
extension AgentServer {

    func analysisTools() -> [[String: Any]] {
        let rateText = AnalysisFaces.rateName
        let subjectsRate = AnalysisSubjects.rateName
        return [
            // It mirrors what the Analyzing sheet's command (CJ2b, Clip ▸ Split
            // at Shot Changes) reads: a media's analysis on this Mac,
            // made or reused. `get_transcript` is its counterpart for words.
            // A read: no op, no `scope`, no undo step. `masks` (CO1), `faces`
            // (CJ3) and `subjects` (VR1) have no menu or pane that makes them:
            // a cut-out clip draws masks, and View ▸ Show Subjects
            // (SubjectsOverlay) draws the faces and subjects already cached;
            // nothing reads `sound_events` (FC3) until Find Clips (FC4).
            tool(
                "get_media_analysis",
                "Answers an analysis of one media file, or of the part of it one clip plays, "
                    + "made ON THIS MAC — no network request, no upload, no API key — and kept "
                    + "per media in the project's cache, so a later call over a window already "
                    + "analysed answers at once. kind \"shots\" finds the hard cuts: cuts is "
                    + "[{frame, source}] sorted by time, frame the media's frame index and "
                    + "source its presentation time in the media's own SOURCE ticks (600000 "
                    + "per second, of the file played forwards), with count. A cut inside a "
                    + "gradual dissolve is not reported, and a single flash frame is not a "
                    + "cut; a dissolve between flat-coloured pictures (slides, title cards) can "
                    + "show as one cut. kind \"masks\" finds a person's outline in every frame "
                    + "(Vision's person segmentation, on the Mac) and answers its runs, never "
                    + "pixels: mask_size [w, h] (the masks' own size), frames (frames held in "
                    + "the window), subject_found (whether any frame holds a person: at least "
                    + "0.5 % of the mask above half), count and runs [{from, to, subject_found, "
                    + "frames}] in SOURCE ticks — a run is consecutive analysed frames that "
                    + "agree on subject_found. Remove Background (Clip ▸ Remove Background, the "
                    + "Clip tab's Picture ▸ Background section, set_video cutout) draws them, "
                    + "and analyze_cutout makes a cut-out clip's masks and says where they "
                    + "stand. kind \"faces\" finds every face "
                    + "(Vision's face rectangles and landmarks, on the Mac) at \(rateText) "
                    + "samples a second of source time and answers rate, count and samples "
                    + "[{source, frame, faces: [{box: [x, y, w, h], confidence, roll, yaw, "
                    + "mouth_gap, mouth_width}]}]: source the sample's instant in SOURCE ticks, "
                    + "frame the presentation time of the frame it read (the first at or after "
                    + "source, within one sample) or null; box 0…1 of the upright picture from "
                    + "its top-left; roll and yaw in radians; mouth_gap the inner lips' height "
                    + "and mouth_width the outer lips' width, each over the face box's height "
                    + "(gap over width is how open the mouth is). Faces are ordered left to "
                    + "right and carry no identity: follow one by its box from sample to "
                    + "sample. Values are rounded to 4 decimals; null where Vision gave none. "
                    + "A sample row with one face is about 176 bytes (221 with clip), so one "
                    + "answer holds about 296 s of samples (236 s with clip), less when more "
                    + "faces are in frame: read a longer media in from/to windows of at most "
                    + "that, e.g. 2 minutes. kind \"sound_events\" listens to the media's "
                    + "first sound track (Apple's Sound Analysis classifier, on the Mac) in "
                    + "windows of \(SoundEvents.windowTicks) ticks (1.5 s) every "
                    + "\(SoundEvents.hopTicks) (0.75 s) and answers window and hop (ticks), "
                    + "groups [{name, labels, first_class, threshold}] — laughter, applause, "
                    + "cheering, crowd, music, speech, each the classifier labels it is the "
                    + "highest confidence of; none is first_class yet, so read the values as "
                    + "hints, never alone as a finding, and threshold is null — count and "
                    + "windows [{source, laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, music, speech}]: "
                    + "source the window's start in SOURCE ticks and each group's confidence "
                    + "0…1, rounded to 4 decimals, null where the classifier gave none (a "
                    + "window running past the sound's end). It needs a media with sound, a "
                    + "video or an audio file; a reversed clip is refused, since its sound "
                    + "plays backwards. A row is about 130 bytes, so one answer holds about "
                    + "an hour of windows. kind \"subjects\" finds people and the regions "
                    + "the eye is drawn to (Vision's upper-body person rectangles and "
                    + "attention-based saliency, on the Mac) at \(subjectsRate) samples a "
                    + "second, each sample instant also a faces sample, and answers rate, count "
                    + "and samples [{source, frame, people: [{box: [x, y, w, h], confidence}], "
                    + "salient: [{box, confidence}]}], boxes as faces' and ordered left to "
                    + "right, with no identity; a person box covers the head and shoulders. A "
                    + "row with one person and one salient box is about 177 bytes (222 with "
                    + "clip), so one answer holds about 294 s of samples (235 s with clip). "
                    + "View ▸ Show Subjects draws the selected clip's faces and subjects at the "
                    + "playhead from what is cached and never analyses. With "
                    + "clip, from and to default to and are held inside "
                    + "the clip's played window, and each cut, sample or window also has clip_time "
                    + "(ticks from "
                    + "the clip's start, in its playing direction — through its speed, ramp "
                    + "and reversal) and timeline (the clip's start plus clip_time). cached "
                    + "says whether the answer came from the cache alone; run "
                    + "({queued_at, started_at, ended_at}, seconds of process uptime) is "
                    + "present only when this call ran the analysis. size is the media's "
                    + "upright picture size; stamp what the cache was made with. A call waits "
                    + "at most \(Int(AnalysisLane.callWaitLimit)) s and then refuses naming "
                    + "how much of the window was covered — what was covered is kept, so call "
                    + "again to continue; an answer over 512 KiB of cuts, runs, samples or "
                    + "windows is "
                    + "refused naming the largest to that fits. It edits nothing and makes no "
                    + "undo step.",
                [
                    "media": [
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "The media whose picture or sound to analyse — exactly "
                            + "one of media and clip.",
                    ],
                    "clip": [
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "A media clip: its media analysed over the part the "
                            + "clip plays — exactly one of media and clip.",
                    ],
                    "kind": [
                        "type": "string", "enum": AnalysisKind.mediaAnalysisKinds.map(\.rawValue),
                        "description": "What to find: shots, the hard cuts; masks, a person's "
                            + "masks' runs; faces, every face per sample (box, roll, yaw, "
                            + "mouth); sound_events, laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, "
                            + "music and speech per window of sound; subjects, people and "
                            + "salient regions per sample.",
                    ],
                    "from": [
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "Where to start, in the media's SOURCE ticks (the file "
                            + "played forwards, 600000 per second), not snapped: 0, or the "
                            + "clip's played window's start, by default.",
                    ],
                    "to": [
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "Where to stop (not included), in the media's SOURCE "
                            + "ticks: the media's end, or the clip's played window's end, by "
                            + "default; must be after from.",
                    ],
                ], required: ["kind"]),
            // Mirrors Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes
            // (EditorViewController+ShotSplit.swift): the same planner,
            // `ShotSplit`, waiting where the menu shows the Analyzing sheet.

/// The catalog row of `get_timeline_transcript` (spec §11 TX-13; road map
/// "creator-jobs" TX1), spliced in by `creatorTools()`.
extension AgentServer {

    func transcriptTools() -> [[String: Any]] {
        [
            // It mirrors the words the Transcript tab (TX2a) will show: the
            // edited container's heard words, read on this Mac once per media
            // (`TranscriptFill`). `get_transcript` stays one clip. A read: no
            // op, no `scope`, no undo step.
            tool(
                "get_timeline_transcript",
                "Answers every word HEARD on the timeline (or inside the nest set_scope has "
                    + "open), in timeline order, nested clips included: words is [{text, start, "
                    + "end, clip, track, media, engine, filler, speaker?, editable, why?, id, "
                    + "cut_start, cut_end}], "
                    + "times in TIMELINE ticks (600000 per second), ordered by start, then end, "
                    + "then the front track first. A clip that is muted, soloed out or at volume "
                    + "0 is not heard and gives no words. track is the timeline track the word "
                    + "plays on (a nested word's is its nest clip's). editable is false, with "
                    + "why, for a word inside a nest, under a transition or on a locked track. "
                    + "id {nest_path, media, source, k} names the word across edits: the nest "
                    + "clips it plays through, its media, its start in the media's SOURCE ticks "
                    + "as the recogniser put it and k, counting earlier words with the same "
                    + "three (0 unless one piece of the source plays twice). An engine apple "
                    + "word's start is where its sound begins, read from the media's voice and "
                    + "waveform caches; until the voice cache exists it is the recogniser's, "
                    + "often early, and notes says so. cut_start and cut_end are the range the "
                    + "Transcript tab cuts that word by when it alone is deleted, snapped to "
                    + "frames: from the word's onset (where its sound starts, read from the voice "
                    + "cache) to the next word's onset, at most 1 s past the word's end, widened "
                    + "over any other track's word it would cut into. To cut a run of words, call "
                    + "ripple_delete_ranges once with one range from its first word's cut_start to "
                    + "its last word's cut_end. pauses is [{start, end, cut_start, cut_end, clip, "
                    + "track, media, follows, precedes}]: each silence over 1 s between two words "
                    + "of one clip, read from the voice cache, start and end where it runs, follows "
                    + "and precedes the ids of the words before and after it, one row per pause "
                    + "whose word before is in words; cut_start and cut_end are what the Transcript "
                    + "tab cuts when that pause is deleted (0.2 s kept at each end, snapped to "
                    + "frames): shorten one with ripple_delete_ranges [[cut_start, cut_end]]. "
                    + "Each media's words come from its cached "
                    + "transcript (engine assemblyai) when it has a current one, else this "
                    + "Mac's own recogniser, which reads the WHOLE file once (about 0.7 s per "
                    + "minute of speech on an M2 Max) and keeps it in the project's cache, so a "
                    + "later call answers at once. It NEVER makes a network request and needs no "
                    + "API key. media is [{media, engine, language, fillers_reported}] for each "
                    + "media read; no_words lists the media clips that cannot be read, "
                    + "[{clip, nest_path, tag, reason}]; notes names two clips carrying the same "
                    + "speech, says when the words were not transcribed with filler words and "
                    + "names a media whose word starts are not yet moved to their sound. "
                    + "filler is true for um, uh, hmm, mhm, uh-huh, ah, huh, hm, m, er and erm. "
                    + "With from or to it answers only the words that overlap that part of the "
                    + "timeline (a word across an edge whole), echoed as from and to. At most "
                    + "2000 words come back: then truncated is true and next_from is where to "
                    + "call again (pass it as from; a word overlapping it may come back again "
                    + "with the same id). It edits nothing and makes no undo step.",
                [
                    "from": [
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "Where on the TIMELINE to start reading, in ticks "
                            + "(600000 per second), snapped to frames; the timeline's start by "
                            + "default. A word across this edge comes back whole.",
                    ],
                    "to": [
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "Where on the TIMELINE to stop reading, in ticks, "

                            + "from.",
                    ],
                    "tracks": [
                        "type": "array", "items": ["type": "integer"],
                        "description": "Only the words playing on these timeline tracks (ids "

                    "language": [

/// The Analyzing sheet (spec §11 CJ-28; road map "creator-jobs" CJ2b): up
/// while the analysis a menu command plans with is made on this Mac, one row
/// per media whose request missed the cache — its file name, a determinate
/// bar, and "Waiting" until the job's first frame, then "NN %", then "Done".
/// The first command is Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes (CJ-29); any kind whose
/// result a command plans with comes through here (CO-6 amends it for a
/// render-substituted kind). A tool call shows no sheet and waits.
///
/// **One owner.** The sheet wants every row's request under one lane owner
/// (alive while the document is open; `settled` tells the document its
/// package changed) when it appears, and releases it in `viewDidDisappear` —
/// its ONE release, on every exit: Stop, landing, failure, the window
/// closing. A disappearance with no outcome and no Stop (the window ordered
/// out, as a minimize does) clears `didStart`, so the next `viewDidAppear`
/// wants again what has not landed and restarts the poll. What a job already
/// published stays cached (CJ-21).
///
/// **Polled, not told:** a 0.1 s `Timer` in the `.common` modes reads
/// `AnalysisLane.progress(of:)` and `run(of:)`. When every run has landed, or
/// one failed, the sheet keeps the outcome and dismisses itself; `finished`
/// is called once, on the main queue's next turn after `viewDidDisappear`
/// (`AudioSyncSheetController`'s reason: the window still reports the sheet
/// attached while it disappears). Stop only dismisses and calls nothing, so
/// no edit lands. While the sheet is attached every editor action validates
/// false (`EditorViewController.validateUserInterfaceItem`).
final class AnalyzingSheetController: NSViewController {
    struct Row {
        let name: String
        let request: AnalysisRequest
    }

    enum Outcome {
        case landed
        case failed(name: String, why: String)
    }

    static let pollInterval: TimeInterval = 0.1

    private let document: ProjectDocument
    private let command: String
    private let rows: [Row]
    private let finished: (Outcome) -> Void
    private let lane = AnalysisLane.shared
    private let owner: Int

    private var bars: [NSProgressIndicator] = []
    private var statuses: [NSTextField] = []
    /// Set in `loadView`; implicitly unwrapped for exactly that reason
    /// (app/CLAUDE.md).
    private var stopButton: NSButton!
    private var hiddenButton: NSButton!

    private var timer: Timer?
    private var didStart = false
    private var reappearing = false
    private var answered = false
    private var stopped = false
    private var outcome: Outcome?

<key>LSMinimumSystemVersion</key>
	<string>26.0</string>
	<key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key>
	<string>Frame Job records the camera you choose, into a file of its own. Nothing is sent anywhere.</string>
	<key>NSHighResolutionCapable</key>
	<true/>
	<key>NSHumanReadableCopyright</key>
	<string></string>
	<key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key>
	<string>Frame Job records the microphone you choose alongside a screen recording, into a file of its own beside the movie. Nothing is sent anywhere.</string>
	<key>NSPrincipalClass</key>
	<string>NSApplication</string>
	<key>SUFeedURL</key>
	<string>$(RC_SPARKLE_FEED_URL:default=)</string>
	<key>SUPublicEDKey</key>
	<string>$(RC_SPARKLE_PUBLIC_KEY:default=)</string>
	<key>UTExportedTypeDeclarations</key>
        NSHighResolutionCapable: true
        ATSApplicationFontsPath: Fonts
        NSHumanReadableCopyright: ""
        # Sparkle's feed and EdDSA public key (spec §11 PUB-6, PUB-8): set in
        # Distribution alone, empty in Debug and Release (PUB-7). No
        # SUEnableAutomaticChecks and no SUAutomaticallyUpdate: Sparkle's own
        # defaults apply (PUB-9).
        SUFeedURL: "$(RC_SPARKLE_FEED_URL:default=)"
        SUPublicEDKey: "$(RC_SPARKLE_PUBLIC_KEY:default=)"
        # File ▸ New Recording… (road map 3, R1c) — the microphone half of a
        # recording, which speech never needed (the speech engine reads an
        # extracted file). The microphone takes TWO things, and this key is one:
        # NSMicrophoneUsageDescription, or AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess and
        # the first AVCaptureDeviceInput CRASH the app; and under the hardened
        # runtime the entitlement com.apple.security.device.audio-input
        # (`entitlements` below), without which the grant is refused however
        # the person answers the prompt. Screen Recording has neither key nor
        # entitlement: its prompt is triggered by the first capture or by
        # CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess().
        NSMicrophoneUsageDescription:
          Frame Job records the microphone you choose alongside a screen recording, into
          a file of its own beside the movie. Nothing is sent anywhere.
        # The camera half of a recording (camera-recording CR1a, spec §11 CAM-3)
        # takes the same two things as the microphone: this key, without which
        # AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess(for: .video) and the first camera
        # AVCaptureDeviceInput CRASH the app, and the entitlement
        # com.apple.security.device.camera (`entitlements` below). No
        # NSCameraUseContinuityCameraDeviceType: CR0's D2 listed the iPhone's
        # Continuity Camera without it.
        NSCameraUsageDescription:
          Frame Job records the camera you choose, into a file of its own. Nothing is
          sent anywhere.
        UTExportedTypeDeclarations:
          - UTTypeIdentifier: com.kgalligan.framejob-project
            UTTypeDescription: Frame Job Project
            UTTypeConformsTo: [com.apple.package]
            UTTypeTagSpecification:
              public.filename-extension: [framejob]
          # The Graphic dialog's Export… (spec §11 G-46 (d)). Data and content,
          # not a zip (spec §11 G-47 (g)), so a browser's "open safe files" and
          # the Finder leave it whole for Frame Job to import.
	<key>com.apple.security.device.audio-input</key>
	<key>com.apple.security.device.camera</key>
    /// `.notDetermined` asks, and denied, restricted or unknown opens the
    /// pane — the system never prompts twice for it.
    static func microphoneStep(_ status: AVAuthorizationStatus) -> Step {
        switch status {
        case .authorized: return .proceed
        case .notDetermined: return .ask
        case .denied, .restricted: return .openPane
        @unknown default: return .openPane
        }
    }

    /// System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording.
    static let screenRecordingPaneURL = URL(
        string: "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_ScreenCapture")

    /// System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Microphone.
    static let microphonePaneURL = URL(
        string: "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_Microphone")

    /// System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Camera (camera-recording CR1c).
    static let cameraPaneURL = URL(
        string: "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_Camera")

    /// What a note adds once the pane has been opened.
    static let paneOpenedSentence = " System Settings is open at that pane."

    /// The screen note after the pane opened: the pane sentence stays the
    /// PREFIX, and `launchClause` stays last.
    static var screenRecordingOpenedNote: String {
        screenRecordingPaneSentence + paneOpenedSentence + launchClause
    }

    /// The microphone note after its pane opened: the refusal's head and
    /// fix, the opened sentence, then `launchClause`.
    static func microphoneOpenedNote(_ status: AVAuthorizationStatus) -> String {
        "The microphone is not granted to Frame Job (status: \(name(of: status))). "
            + "Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Microphone, then relaunch."
            + paneOpenedSentence + launchClause
    }

    // MARK: Input Monitoring (road map creator-jobs CU6, spec §11 CU-3, CU-62)

    /// `CGPreflightListenEventAccess()` — whether this process may listen to key-downs (CU-S1
    /// `grant_api=cg`). A shell launch reads the terminal's grant, as Screen Recording does.
    static var inputMonitoringGranted: Bool { CGPreflightListenEventAccess() }

    /// CU-3's sentence: no "then relaunch" (CU0b measured none is needed).
    static let inputMonitoringPaneSentence =
        "Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ "
        + "Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring."

    /// `record_screen`'s and the recorder's refusal: the pane sentence, then `launchClause`.
    static var inputMonitoringRefusal: String { inputMonitoringPaneSentence + launchClause }

    /// What the panel's note adds: no prompt shows and Frame Job is not listed until a person
    /// adds it (CU0b, the owner's JOB-29 run).
    static let inputMonitoringAddSentence = " If Frame Job is not in its list, add it with +."

    /// The panel's note after a press: the pane sentence, the add sentence, the opened sentence
    /// when System Settings opened, then `launchClause`.
    static func inputMonitoringNote(opened: Bool) -> String {
        inputMonitoringPaneSentence + inputMonitoringAddSentence
            + (opened ? paneOpenedSentence : "") + launchClause
    }

    /// Input Monitoring: `screenStep`'s table — granted goes on; a shell launch always asks; a
    /// launchd-owned press that has asked before opens the pane; else ask (CU-62).
    static func inputMonitoringStep(granted: Bool, asked: Bool, launchedByLaunchd: Bool) -> Step {
        if granted { return .proceed }
        if !launchedByLaunchd { return .ask }
        if asked { return .openPane }

/// first six carry 5c's sentences; the last four are this client's own.
    enum ClientError: LocalizedError, Equatable {
        case noNetwork
        case keyRefused(Int)
        case account(String)
        case request(String)
        case server(Int)
        case transcript(String)
        case redirected(Int)
        case timedOut
        case cancelled
        case malformed(String)
        case submissionUnresolved(authenticationStatus: Int?)

        var errorDescription: String? {
            switch self {
            case .noNetwork:
                return "No network connection"
            case .keyRefused:
                return "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings"
            case .account(let sentence):
                return sentence
            case .request(let sentence):
                return sentence
            case .server(let code):
                return "AssemblyAI answered \(code)"
            case .transcript(let sentence):
                return sentence
            case .redirected(let code):
                return "AssemblyAI answered \(code) and asked to be redirected, which Frame Job "
                    + "does not follow: the API key would go to another host."
            case .timedOut:
                return "AssemblyAI did not finish the transcript in the time allowed."
            case .cancelled:
                return "The transcription was cancelled."
            case .malformed(let what):
                return "AssemblyAI's answer could not be read: \(what)"
            case .submissionUnresolved(let authenticationStatus):
                let warning = "AssemblyAI may have created a transcript, but Frame Job could not "
                    + "recover its ID. Check your AssemblyAI dashboard before retrying; the "
                    + "transcript may still be retained."
                if authenticationStatus != nil {
                    return "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings. "
                        + warning
                }
                return warning
            }
        }
    }

    /// A finished transcript and the bytes of its `words` array exactly as
    /// served — never re-serialised, because a `0.98` does not survive that
    /// (`MediaTranscript`'s header argues it).
    struct Fetched {
        let response: TranscriptResponse
        let wordsJSON: Data
    }
